Court No. - 66
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 41559 of 2024

Applicant :- Ajeet Kumar
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Chandan Yadav,Deepesh Kumar Ojha,Dipanshu Kushwaha

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1. Heard Sri Dipanshu Kushwaha, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Shatrughna Yadav,
learned Aga for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
272 of 2024, under Sections 366, 376, 420, 323 and 506 IPC, Police Station- Gambhirpur, District- Azamgarh, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged on 16.07.2024 against applicant and others and according to FIR, friendship of the informant was developed with the applicant and on 04.09.2023, applicant along with his three associates had taken her to Mirzapur and on the basis of fake notary certificate performed marriage with her and thereafter he along with his three associates committed rape upon her and thereafter he turned her out.
It is further mentioned in the FIR that on 02.07.2024 applicant made a demand of Rs. 1 lakh and threatened her to break the marriage.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that informant i.e. victim of the case is major lady and she is wife of the applicant and fact of marriage has been admitted by the victim even in the FIR itself and as victim is major and wife of the applicant, therefore, no offence under Section 376 IPC is made out against the applicant.
5.

He further submitted that however, as per victim, applicant and three others committed rape upon her but the alleged rape was committed on 04.09.2023 and FIR was lodged on 16.07.2024 i.e.
after 10 months and this fact suggests that FIR is based on false and frivolous facts.
He further submitted that during investigation, other named accused persons have been exonerated by the Investigating Officer and charge sheet was filed only against the applicant.
6. He further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 17.07.2024.
7. Per contra, learned AGA however, opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. However, as per allegation, applicant along with three others committed rape upon the victim i.e.
informant of the case on 04.09.2023 but admittedly victim is major lady and FIR of the present case was lodged on 16.07.2024 i.e. after 10 months.
10. Further, it reflects, applicant is the husband of the victim and even victim admitted this fact in the FIR itself.
11. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 17.07.2024.
12. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
13. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant- Ajeet Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from Ajeet Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21906132/
2 disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
15. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

16. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
